title: length-tier packing and cost-aware slotting to minimize padding and improve KV locality
author: Maya Gupta
release_notes: Introduce length-tier packing with cost-aware slotting: reduces padding waste and improves KV cache hit stability. Opt-in via scheduler.packing.length_tiers and rollout metric gating.
description:
Summary:
This PR introduces a length-tier packing algorithm plus a cost-aware slotting policy in the runtime scheduler to reduce padding overhead and improve KV-cache locality for mixed-length workloads. The change is opt-in (scheduler.packing.enabled=false by default) and designed for minimal risk: it does not modify model kernels or public API surface.

Motivation:
We observed persistent padding waste in multi-tenant traffic with broad seq-length distributions. Padding causes extra token work, worsens latency tail, and reduces effective KV-cache reuse because coalesced slots mix requests from very different sequence prefixes. Existing bucketing heuristics were either too coarse or induced oscillation under bursty traffic. We need a packing scheme that: (1) minimizes per-batch padding cost, (2) preserves KV cache locality across similar prefixes, and (3) plays nicely with continuous batching and autoscaling.

Design overview:
- Length tiers: incoming requests are quantized into a small set (configurable, default 6) of "length tiers" (very-short, short, mid, mid-long, long, very-long). Tiers are defined by percentile anchors computed from an EWMA sketch of recent seq-lengths.
- Slotting (cost-aware): the scheduler maintains slots sized for a target output token budget. When forming a batch, requests are preferentially placed into slots with the closest upper-tier bound to avoid unnecessary padding. Each candidate slot has a dynamic cost estimate: padding_cost + kv_locality_penalty. The latter penalizes mixing requests whose prefix keys differ (hash distance heuristics) to preserve KV cache hit rates.
- Backfill and spill policy: small/unfilled slots are allowed a short grace window (configurable ms) to accept compatible arrivals; after that they can be spilled into a fallback merge policy to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Integration with continuous batching: the packer attaches metadata (tier_id, slot_id) so runtime backends can prioritize KV-cache placement and kernel selection. No change to model weights or serialized model artifacts.

Implementation details:
- New scheduler module: src/runtime/scheduler/length_tier_packer.rs implements tier computation, slot descriptors, and placement heuristics.
- Cache-aware fingerprinting: src/runtime/kv/cache_key_finder.rs adds an optional lightweight prefix fingerprint used to score kv_locality_penalty. The fingerprint uses the first N bytes of normalized prefix tokens to avoid heavy hashing.
- Configuration: config/defaults.yaml adds scheduler.packing.length_tiers, scheduler.packing.grace_ms, scheduler.packing.max_slot_padding_ratio.
- Metrics and traces: observability hooks added in src/observability/metrics.rs and tracing spans in the packer so we can track padding_saved, kv_locality_hit_ratio, slot_utilization. Dashboards updated in docs/observability/length-tier-dashboard.md.
- Tests + benchmarks: added unit tests (tests/unit/test_length_tier_packer.rs), integration tests with continuous batching harness (tests/batching/length_tier_integration_test.py), and a microbenchmark simulation (benchmarks/length_tier_simulation.json).

Key files changed (high-level):
- src/runtime/scheduler/length_tier_packer.rs
- src/runtime/kv/cache_key_finder.rs
- src/observability/metrics.rs
- config/defaults.yaml
- tests/unit/test_length_tier_packer.rs
- tests/batching/length_tier_integration_test.py
- docs/observability/length-tier-dashboard.md
- benchmarks/length_tier_simulation.json
- pkg/python/redwood/adapter/packing_adapter.py

Benchmarks (internal cluster, Ampere A100 equiv):
- Workload: synthetic mix of very-short(30%), short(25%), mid(20%), long(25%) sequences; open-loop arrival at 1200 req/s, model = gpt-medium-6B.
- Baseline: current percentile-bucket strategy. Packer enabled with 6 tiers and default costs.
- Results (P50, P95 generation latency for 512 token windows, cost = compute tokens):
  - Baseline P50: 34.2 ms, P95: 129.3 ms, compute tokens/sec cost baseline = 1.00
  - This PR P50: 30.9 ms (9.6% improvement), P95: 115.1 ms (10.9% improvement), compute tokens/sec cost = 0.88 (12% token savings due to less padding)
- KV-cache locality: measured as fraction of continuation requests hitting existing KV shards; improved from 0.62 -> 0.78 in simulation.

Rollout and gating:
- Feature is opt-in. Default off for safety.
- Canary plan: enable for 5% of traffic on dedicated pool with realtime metric gating on padding_saved and kv_locality_hit_ratio; automatic rollback if P95 regression > 5% or errors increase.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests cover tier assignment and slot selection heuristics, fuzz tests for edge cases around boundary seq-lengths.
- Integration test simulates continuous batching with varying arrival bursts and verifies no deadlocks and acceptable slot spill behaviour.
- Bench harness run against staging with deterministic seed; results captured in benchmarks/length_tier_simulation.json.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of length tiers and slotting
- [x] Lightweight KV prefix fingerprint and scoring hook
- [x] Metrics + tracing for rollout observability
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks showing latency/cost wins
- [x] Opt-in config and canary gating plan documented

Related work:
- This complements earlier bucketed-batching efforts but focuses on minimizing padding cost while preserving KV locality; see ENG-1321 for prior percentile bucketer.
- Linear: ENG-1985 tracks production rollout and metric dashboards.

Notes on risk and mitigation:
- Risk: mis-tuned tier boundaries could increase fragmentation and reduce throughput. Mitigation: EWMA anchor updates are rate-limited and changes are exposed as metrics; rollout gating prevents noisy changes.
- Risk: fingerprint collisions could misrepresent KV locality. Mitigation: fingerprint is intentionally small and used only for scoring, not for correctness of keying.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2026-03-05 after approvals from Owen Park and Zara Li. CI green after a lint failure was fixed in a small follow-up commit.

If reviewers want: I can follow up with a short RFC doc describing the cost model mathematics used for slot scoring (padding_cost + alpha * locality_penalty) and provide a tuning guide for ops teams.

review_comments: Owen Park: Nice work, Maya. Can you clarify how EWMA anchors are initialized after a cold restart? We should avoid a transient where almost everything maps to 'very-long'.

Maya Gupta: Good catch. Anchors are initialized from the last persisted snapshot (if present) and fall back to a short-default distribution (percentiles from historical traffic profile) to avoid the long transient. I added a comment and unit test to cover the cold start path.
Zara Li: The kv_locality_penalty seems sensitive to the fingerprint length. Have you tried 8 vs 16 bytes? What's the perf cost?

Maya Gupta: I ran a microbenchmark; 8 bytes gives nearly identical locality discrimination vs 16 for our corpora but is cheaper to compute/compare. Default set to 8; adjustable via config. Results added to benchmarks/length_tier_simulation.json.
Rajesh Kumar: CI failed on lint initially. After fix, everything passed locally. Approving once CI green.
Owen Park: Approving; pls ensure rollout gating is enabled in the default release manifest (off by default, but present).
